_readme: The editorial layer. scripts/fetch-tles.mjs pulls the CelesTrak 'active' catalog ONCE,
then filters it locally against every source below. Adding a company costs zero extra
HTTP requests — one fetch a day covers the whole roster however long it gets.
HOW TO POPULATE THIS FILE: run scripts/seed-from-gcat.mjs. GCAT records manufacture at
the level of the operating location — the factory — rather than the headquarters parent
company, which is exactly the distinction this project needs. HQ data says BlackSky is
Virginia; factory data says the satellites were built in Tukwila. The script writes
CANDIDATES to data/gcat-washington.json; a human folds them in here with a signature.
It will not write to this file, on purpose.
much larger and much harder claim; this roster does not attempt it.
GCAT DOES reach propulsion. Its satcat.tsv carries both Manufacturer and Motor,
and Aerojet Rocketdyne/Redmond is a GCAT organization at 47.67N 122.12W. So
Washington-built thrusters on otherwise non-WA spacecraft ARE discoverable — the
seed script reports them separately as role:'propulsion'. Whether they belong on
the map is an editorial call, not a data limitation. Counting them would make the
Washington footprint far larger and the claim far broader.
WASHINGTON-BUILT MEANS: place of manufacture or final assembly. Not headquarters, not
operator, not launch site — nothing here launched from Washington, and 'Washington-
launched' would be false.
match   : regex tested against the object name (case-insensitive)
ids     : explicit NORAD numbers, for craft whose names give nothing away
exclude : regex to drop false positives
class   : drives the icon on the sky dome — sat, broadband, imaging, servicer, tug,
datacenter, cubesat, relay, bus, rocketbody
limit   : cap; when a source matches more, the script samples evenly across planes
verify  : what a human still needs to confirm. Not optional reading.
PROVENANCE: basis / source_url / verified_by / verified_on must ALL be filled before
this goes on a screen. scripts/fetch-tles.mjs prints an audit and stamps verified:false
into data/tles.json for anything unsigned, so an unverified claim can never ship silently.

definition._: The canonical statement of what this project claims. Everything else follows from it. Space Northwest owns this; change it here and the page copy should be updated to match.
definition.washington_built: A spacecraft counts as Washington-built if its primary structure and bus were manufactured in Washington State, OR if it underwent final integration in Washington State.
decision_order: 1. Final integration in WA -> counts. Record the facility.

2. Bus manufactured in WA, integrated elsewhere -> counts, but tag it. The Loft Orbital YAM satellites are this case: LeoStella bus from Tukwila, integration elsewhere. Defensible, but say 'bus built in Washington' rather than implying the whole spacecraft.

3. Subsystem or component only (propulsion, antennas, avionics) -> does NOT count as Washington-built. Aerojet Rocketdyne's Redmond propulsion is the large case here. It is reachable through GCAT's Motor field, so it is an editorial exclusion, not a data limitation.
4. Headquarters, operator, owner, or launch site -> never sufficient on its own. BlackSky is a Virginia company whose satellites are Tukwila-built; the factory is what counts.
5. Multi-site production -> name the site where final integration occurs. If that is unknown, name the primary production facility and say so in 'basis'.
definition.ownership_changes: The factory is what counts, not who owns it. LeoStella's acquisition by BlackSky in Nov 2024 does not change the status of anything built in Tukwila before or after.
definition.operational: Present in the CelesTrak active catalog. Verified in practice on 2026-08-31: seven spacecraft with sound Washington attributions in GCAT — HuskySat-1, Blue Ring Pathfinder, both Arkyds, both OrbWeavers, MAST — were all absent from the active catalog and are therefore excluded. Being Washington-built is not sufficient; the spacecraft has to still be up there. DECAY_DATE and OPS_STATUS_CODE are fetched from SATCAT and could tighten this further.
evidence_standard: Each attribution needs at least one of: a company statement or press release, a regulatory filing, or a GCAT factory-level manufacturer record.
Trade press alone is a lead, not a source. Record it in 'basis' and keep looking.
The source goes in source_url. The person who accepted it goes in verified_by, with the date in verified_on.
Anything unsigned is stamped verified:false and the page says so on screen.
never_claim: 'Washington-launched' — there is no orbital launch site in Washington.
Historical manufacturing totals presented as current counts.
A percentage of the global fleet without a source, denominator and date.
